title: A feed uses more RAM than expected
description: Your hybrid feed already handles celebrity fan-out. Now each follower's cached feed stores complete post objects, so memory is growing quickly and a text edit requires millions of cache writes. Which representation keeps reads efficient without duplicating all the content?

options.text: Keep complete objects but invalidate every follower's entire feed on each edit.
options.explanation: This retains the memory duplication and turns edits into widespread cache misses and rebuilds.

options.text: Store the full post in the follow graph so each feed can join it there.
options.explanation: Moving content duplication into relationship storage does not solve ownership or update fan-out, and mixes unrelated access patterns.

options.text: Keep capped post-ID lists and batch-hydrate post and author objects from shared caches, over-fetching for filtered items.
options.explanation: Shared objects make edits cheap, while parallel multi-gets keep hydration fast. Over-fetching leaves enough visible items after deleted or blocked posts are removed.

options.text: Read every followed author's recent posts from storage on each request.
options.explanation: That avoids duplicated content but abandons the precomputed read path, restoring hundreds of author lookups per feed request.
